title: an unknown manifest-entry `format` is rejected naming the supported set
why: `format` is a schema DISCRIMINANT — it selects HOW a
registry must read the artifact bytes an entry names (`cuModuleLoadData`
for PTX text vs. a binary cubin/fatbin), so an unrecognized value is
refused rather than handed to the loader as though it were a known
container. Matches the producer of record's vocabulary
(the manifest producer's format set: ptx | cubin | fatbin).
Checked over every declared entry BEFORE any sidecar parse / module load
(this fixture's referenced gravity.ptx/gravity.json need not exist), so
the reject fires with no GPU and no disk I/O beyond the manifest itself —
the manifest-level twin of the duplicate-id structural check.
`cpp_load_manifest` maps to the HOST registry (eagle::cpu::PluginRegistry
::load) — the only C++ manifest loader this CUDA-free driver TU can reach;
the DEVICE registry's identical check (plugin_registry/registry.h:150) is
exercised by the named CUDA-only .cu unit test
PluginRegistryManifestTest.RejectsUnknownManifestFormat
(test_PluginRegistryManifest.cu) — added together with this row's device
counterpart, after an audit found
the format/schema_version device gates untested and this same claim false
An outside-coverage claim here must NAME the
test that provides it, not just gesture at a file.
